item.text:
**5B.1 Result:** mostly weaker. Putin’s 2024 record contains some rhetoric about long-run development and inflation control, but the observable economic model was still war-financed, militarized, inflationary, and patronage-heavy rather than broad-based and sustainable.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Weak pro | Executive Order on Russia's development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets official goals for “sustainable economic and social development,” higher living standards, fair competition, entrepreneurship/private initiative, and technological effectiveness. This is the clearest pro-sustainability statement, but it is aspirational rather than proof of implementation. | 5B.1 |
| Weak pro | Putin: Must pay special attention to containing Russian inflation | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-12 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/putin-must-pay-special-attention-to-containing-russian-inflation-3300567 | Putin publicly prioritized inflation containment and said inflation was trending lower, which supports a limited macro-stability reading. It does not by itself show a broad-based growth strategy. | 5B.1 |
| Against | Analysis-Russia's GDP boost from military spending belies wider economic woes | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-02-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/analysisrussias-gdp-boost-on-military-spending-belies-wider-economic-woes-3295688 | Reuters said the growth rebound relied heavily on state-funded arms and ammunition production and masked problems that hindered living standards. This points toward war-driven output rather than sustainable prosperity. | 5B.1 |
| Against | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | The economy grew across many sectors and unemployment was at a record low, but Reuters explicitly linked the expansion to military production. That is evidence of headline growth without a broad, civilian-led prosperity model. | 5B.1 |
| Against | Analysis-Russia braces for more tax rises to fund the Ukraine war | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-10-31 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/analysisrussia-braces-for-more-tax-rises-to-fund-the-ukraine-war-3693480 | Economists said Russia would need more tax increases to finance ballooning military spending. That looks like extraction to sustain war rather than a durable broad-based prosperity strategy. | 5B.1 |
| Against | Putin urges 'balanced' central bank rate decision for overheating economy | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/putin-says-russias-economy-is-overheating-inflation-is-worrying-3781400 | Putin acknowledged overheating and worrying inflation, which suggests the 2024 model was straining households and macro stability. This is closer to crisis management than sustainable prosperity. | 5B.1 |
| Against | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says corruption is pervasive and that the regime sustains itself through the distribution of economic assets to allies and protection from prosecution in return for loyalty. That is classic rent extraction and loyalty buying. | 5B.1 |

**Assessment**
- The strongest pro evidence is rhetorical: formal development goals and inflation containment.
- The strongest empirical evidence points the other way: growth was driven by military production, taxes were being raised to finance war, inflation was still a concern, and corruption/patronage remained central.

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of a real pivot toward diversified, private-sector-led, anti-corruption, long-horizon prosperity creation.
- I also did not find strong evidence that the growth model was broad-based in the civilian economy; the best available growth figures were repeatedly described as war-driven and distortionary.
